item.text: I’ll inspect the repository’s Ubuntu lifecycle data and its existing tests, write the required checkpoint early, then make the focused data change and run the relevant existing tests.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "mkdir -p .codex-role-output && cat > .codex-role-output/checkpoint.md <<'EOF'
# Checkpoint

Issue: add Ubuntu 20.04 extended support through 2030-04-01 and Ubuntu 22.04 lifecycle metadata (standard support through 2027-04-01; extended support through 2032-04-01).

Repository inspection is underway. No implementation files have been changed yet.
EOF
find . -type f \\( -name '*.go' -o -name '*.json' -o -name '*.yaml' -o -name '*.yml' \\) -print | xargs grep -n -i -E 'ubuntu|eol|end.of.life|extended support' | head -220"

item.text: The Debian/Ubuntu scanner takes the reported release string directly and handles Ubuntu package scanning by family, so adding `22.04` to `GetEOL` makes it a known lifecycle release without a separate version switch. I’ve updated the Ubuntu EOL table; next I’m running the existing `config` tests and checking the final diff.
